So I decided after this election that I need a more comprehensive approach to donating to things. Here are my thoughts. I believe in what I call agencied justice. That is that you are liable for your actions and conscious inactions.

So I got to thinking about how to defend my freedom and what my responsibility is. I was already in the habit of donating with the intention of promoting freedom / securing my freedom and my reasoning went like this. If I donate to one cause someone else will donate to the others and thereby I'll have justly protected my freedom. I got to thinking that wasn't quite right. Instead what I did is broke down what is needed to have a free society by concept and then tied an organization to that. Here's the list. The idea is if any one of these disappeared completely, freedom would be lost completely (based on my personal opinion).

Legal Advocacy: EFF.
Alternate sources and record for current events: Wikileaks
Freedom of discussion without subversion of public opinion: Voat.
Ownership of the behavior of our hardware: Linux.
Concern for the needy: Personal
The gospel of Christ: Based on personal beliefs
Law and Order / Legal consistency / Physical Security: 3 percenters.
Money that isn't a free tap for corruption: Bitcoin Foundation.

Other options for some of these are the ACLU, IJ, Gab, Quitter, GNU, BSD, NRA, dash.

I really don't mean to virtue signal. My donations are tiny. I just want to expose you to this concept. I really think that if any one of these crumbled all the others would crumble fast. So I'm taking personal responsibility for each of these by paying (unfortunately nominal) amounts to each of them. I feel like if I didn't I would have a diminished claim for injustice if one of these rights was removed.

I'm going to ask if you would do the same, if you are willing. I would really appreciate it. It will enhance my freedom if you do. Please do. I hope that I am asking nicely because I mean to but I also mean to firmly present its need in as polite a manner as can be. If you will, decide a percentage of your income then give to each of these that you believe has some relevance to your freedom.

Imagine if this was a warning (I don't know that it is), but if you were warned that you need to pay 1% of your income or loose your freedom would you let freedom slip from your fingers over 1% of your pay? The question is what percentage justly secures your freedom.
So I just donated to a few places and want to share my thoughts on the matter

Your statement seems strange to me:

there is no state, no money, no class system

A state is just a territory with a sovereign government. A government is the system by which the state is organized (in this case communism is the system).

A better example of a stateless society would be an anarchy (not chaos, but absence of a system). So for this example, the state is communist.

A communist society still needs a way to exchange goods and services. Money is a flexible way to do that - and money can still be controlled by a central / communal process. Do you want to barter? Do you want to have quotas of allowed "needs"? Do it how you will, but using a currency doesn't break communism. Removing currency from a society simply makes it difficult to exchange things.

And you're right, there is no class system - but classes can still form as a result of any differences between people (employment, race, age, disability, sex, gender, location, etc.).
